newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HORSE RACING-BANS EXTENDED AFTER RACE-RIGGING SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BANS EXTENDED AFTER RACE-RIGGING SCANDAL.

text.p: Hong Kong's Jockey Club extended the suspension of two top trainers, five jockeys and three staff on Thursday in the wake of one of the territory's biggest horse racing scandals.
Trainers Chan Pak-hung and Leung Sik-lun would be banned until May 19, the Jockey Club said.
Jockeys Yim Hin-keung and Choi Chun-wai, and apprentices Ho Wah-lun, Tam Shu-man and Ko Chun-ho were suspended until May 15.
In addition, the club extended indefinitely the suspension of three staff, Terrence Spargo, Jennifer Chapman and Kwok Chin-chuen.
The club, which holds the monopoly on racing and gaming in Hong Kong, was shaken badly last month when five were charged with illegal bookmaking and two trainers and five jockeys suspended.
More than 200 of the territory's anti-graft police stormed Hong Kong's Sha Tin race track on March 16, hauling away 37 people for questioning.
The Jockey Club's chief executive Lawrence Wong said it was stepping up vetting of staff, jockeys and trainers and was confident its reputation remained high despite last month's race-rigging affair.
"We are very determined to keep Hong Kong racing clean," Wong said. "We are constantly looking at how to improve the system."

The Jockey Club, which recently dropped the word "Royal" from its name in preparation for the colony's return to China later this year, is regarded as one of the venerable bastions of the colonial establishment.
Wong said the scandal had not affected betting turnover or damaged the club's reputation.
"If we don't handle the situation, then yes. But the fact we dealt with it and we pro-actively dealth with it, that would help by and large to build public confidence."
